Checklist: 1) Identify all enums, structs, typedefs, and function pointer types defined in grok.h. 2) Exclude externally referenced-but-undefined types. 3) For each type, capture full textual definition and purpose. 4) Map ownership relations based on fields. 5) Associate creation APIs where applicable. 6) Validate completeness, noting unknowns.

functions.name: grk_version
functions.description: Returns the Grok library version string for runtime introspection or logging. Call after grk_initialize or even before if only querying version; no state required is documented.
requirements: None beyond being callable at any time; no parameters or global state required are documented.
Return is a NUL-terminated const char* that should not be freed by the caller.

functions.name: grk_initialize
functions.signature: bool GRK_CALLCONV grk_initialize(const char* pluginPath, uint32_t num_threads)
functions.description: Initializes the Grok library and must be called before any other Grok API calls. Optionally specifies a plugin path and the number of worker threads used by compression/decompression.
requirements: Must be called before any Grok API calls (library-wide precondition).
pluginPath may be NULL or a valid path string (exact requirement not specified; behavior when NULL is unknown).
num_threads is a non-negative 32-bit value; exact valid range is unspecified.
Returns true on success, false on failure; callers should check the return value and avoid using the API on failure.

functions.name: grk_deinitialize
functions.description: De-initializes the Grok library and releases global resources. Typically not necessary to call explicitly, but provided for controlled shutdown.
requirements: Should only be called after a successful grk_initialize (implied).
Do not use Grok API that requires initialization after calling this, unless grk_initialize is called again.

functions.name: grk_object_ref
functions.description: Increments the reference count of a Grok reference-counted object and returns the same object pointer. Use to extend the lifetime across owners.
requirements: obj must be a valid pointer to a live grk_object (opaque) obtained from the API.
Returned pointer aliases obj; caller must later balance with grk_object_unref for each successful ref.

functions.name: grk_object_unref
functions.description: Decrements the reference count of a Grok reference-counted object. When the count reaches zero, the object is destroyed.
requirements: obj must be a valid pointer previously obtained from the API (or NULL is unspecified).
After unref that drops the last reference, the object is destroyed; caller must not use obj afterwards.

functions.name: grk_set_msg_handlers
functions.description: Sets global logging message handlers for info/debug/trace/warn/error messages. Each handler carries an optional client_data pointer passed back on invocation.
requirements: Each function pointer in msg_handlers may be NULL to disable that message type (not explicitly stated; behavior if NULL is unknown).
Client data pointers supplied in msg_handlers must remain valid for the time the handlers can be invoked.
Should be called after grk_initialize and before operations that emit logs, to ensure handlers are installed.

functions.name: grk_image_new
functions.signature: grk_image* GRK_CALLCONV grk_image_new(uint16_t numcmpts, grk_image_comp* cmptparms, GRK_COLOR_SPACE clrspc, bool alloc_data)
functions.description: Creates a new grk_image with the specified number of components, component parameters, and color space. If alloc_data is true, component data buffers are allocated.
requirements: numcmpts specifies the number of components; must be consistent with the cmptparms array length.
cmptparms must point to an array of numcmpts grk_image_comp structs describing each component; fields like w/h/prec/sgnd should be set appropriately.
clrspc must be a valid GRK_COLOR_SPACE value.
If alloc_data is true, the library allocates component data buffers; caller becomes owner of the image and must later release it with grk_object_unref on the image's obj.

functions.name: grk_image_meta_new
functions.description: Creates a new grk_image_meta object holding image metadata such as ICC profile, IPTC, XMP, palette and channel definition.
requirements: Caller must release the returned object by grk_object_unref when no longer needed (the struct contains an embedded grk_object).

functions.name: grk_decompress_init
functions.signature: grk_object* GRK_CALLCONV grk_decompress_init(grk_stream_params* stream_params, grk_decompress_parameters* params)
functions.description: Initializes a decompression codec object for a given input stream and decompression parameters. Returns an opaque grk_object representing the codec.
requirements: Must be called after grk_initialize succeeds.
stream_params must be populated to select exactly one streaming method (file, buffer, or callbacks) as stated by the struct comment.
For callback-based read streams, stream_len is mandatory (per struct comment).
params must point to a grk_decompress_parameters struct; fields control core behavior and I/O callbacks.
Returns nullptr on failure; callers must check and avoid further use on failure.
The returned grk_object must be released with grk_object_unref when done.

functions.name: grk_decompress_update
functions.description: Updates an existing decompression codec with new parameters at runtime.
requirements: codec must be a valid decompression codec object returned by grk_decompress_init.
params must point to a valid grk_decompress_parameters struct.
Returns true on success; callers must handle false (no change applied).

functions.name: grk_decompress_get_progression_state
functions.description: Returns the progression state for a specified tile of a decompression codec. If the tile has not been decompressed yet, the returned struct is all zeros.
requirements: codec must be a valid decompression codec object.
tile_index must reference a valid tile index for the current image; behavior for out-of-range is unspecified.

functions.name: grk_decompress_set_progression_state
functions.description: Sets the progression state for a tile, marking it dirty if appropriate. Returns true if the tile exists in cache and the state marked the tile as dirty.
requirements: codec must be a valid decompression codec object.
state must be populated consistently; fields like num_resolutions/layers_per_resolution should reflect the intended state (details not fully documented).
Return value indicates whether a cache entry existed and was marked dirty; callers should check and react accordingly.

functions.name: grk_decompress_read_header
functions.signature: bool GRK_CALLCONV grk_decompress_read_header(grk_object* codec, grk_header_info* header_info)
functions.description: Parses and reads the JPEG 2000 main codestream header (and JP2 header for JP2) and fills the provided header_info structure with image and coding parameters.
requirements: codec must be a valid decompression codec created with grk_decompress_init.
header_info must be a valid pointer to a grk_header_info structure that the library can write into.
Returns true if the headers are correctly read; false otherwise. Caller must check return value before using header_info fields.

functions.name: grk_decompress_get_tile_image
functions.signature: grk_image* GRK_CALLCONV grk_decompress_get_tile_image(grk_object* codec, uint16_t tile_index, bool wait)
functions.description: Retrieves the decompressed image for a specific tile. If wait is true, the call may block until the tile is ready.
requirements: codec must be a valid decompression codec.
tile_index must be within the image's tile grid; exact bounds are image-dependent.
If wait is false and the tile is not yet decompressed, the returned value may be NULL (behavior not explicitly stated).
Returned grk_image is owned by the codec; lifetime/ownership rules are not fully documented—do not free directly; manage codec lifetime instead.

functions.name: grk_decompress_get_image
functions.description: Returns the decompressed full image associated with the codec, if available.
requirements: codec must be a valid decompression codec.
May return NULL if the image is not yet decompressed or on error (not explicitly stated).
Returned grk_image is managed by the codec; do not free directly.

functions.name: grk_decompress
functions.signature: bool GRK_CALLCONV grk_decompress(grk_object* codec, grk_plugin_tile* tile)
functions.description: Performs decompression using the provided plugin tile structure and the codec state. Intended for plugin-driven decoding stages.
requirements: codec must be a valid decompression codec.
tile must point to a valid grk_plugin_tile struct whose fields match the current decode stage expectations.
Returns true on success; false otherwise.

functions.name: grk_decompress_wait
functions.signature: void GRK_CALLCONV grk_decompress_wait(grk_object* codec, grk_wait_swath* swath)
functions.description: Blocks until an asynchronous decompression completes. If swath is non-NULL, waits until the specified pixel region is available; otherwise waits for the full decode.
requirements: codec must be a valid decompression codec.
If swath is provided, its x/y bounds define a rectangular region in pixel coordinates; tile index fields are set by the library (per struct comment).

functions.name: grk_decompress_tile
functions.signature: bool GRK_CALLCONV grk_decompress_tile(grk_object* codec, uint16_t tile_index)
functions.description: Decompresses a specific tile by index.
requirements: codec must be a valid decompression codec.
tile_index must be a valid tile index for the current image.
Returns true on success; false otherwise.

functions.name: grk_compress_set_default_params
functions.description: Initializes a grk_cparameters structure with sensible defaults for lossless, single-tile compression (precinct 2^15x2^15, code block 64x64, 6 resolutions, LRCP, reversible 5-3, etc.).
requirements: parameters must be a valid pointer to a grk_cparameters struct to be written by the function.
Should be called before customizing fields for compression.

functions.name: grk_compress_init
functions.signature: grk_object* GRK_CALLCONV grk_compress_init(grk_stream_params* stream_params, grk_cparameters* parameters, grk_image* image)
functions.description: Initializes a compression codec for the given output stream, compression parameters, and input image. Returns an opaque grk_object representing the codec.
requirements: Must be called after grk_initialize succeeds.
stream_params must be populated for exactly one streaming method (file, buffer, or callbacks) as per struct comment.
parameters must point to a valid grk_cparameters structure (optionally initialized via grk_compress_set_default_params).
image must be a valid grk_image prepared for compression.
Returns nullptr on failure; check before proceeding. Release the returned codec with grk_object_unref when done.

functions.name: grk_compress
functions.signature: uint64_t GRK_CALLCONV grk_compress(grk_object* codec, grk_plugin_tile* tile)
functions.description: Compresses image data into a JPEG 2000 codestream using a plugin-provided tile representation. Returns the number of bytes written on success, 0 otherwise.
requirements: codec must be a valid compression codec created by grk_compress_init.
tile must be a valid pointer to a grk_plugin_tile structure populated as expected by the current compression stage.
Caller should check for a non-zero return indicating success.

functions.name: grk_dump_codec
functions.signature: void GRK_CALLCONV grk_dump_codec(grk_object* codec, uint32_t info_flag, FILE* output_stream)
functions.description: Dumps codec information to the provided FILE stream for debugging/inspection. info_flag selects the type of information (e.g., GRK_IMG_INFO, GRK_MH_INFO, etc.).
requirements: codec must be a valid codec object (compression or decompression).
output_stream must be a valid FILE* opened for writing.
info_flag should be a combination of defined flags (e.g., GRK_IMG_INFO, GRK_MH_INFO, GRK_TH_INFO, GRK_TCH_INFO, GRK_MH_IND, GRK_TH_IND).

functions.name: grk_set_MCT
functions.signature: bool GRK_CALLCONV grk_set_MCT(grk_cparameters* parameters, const float* encoding_matrix, const int32_t* dc_shift, uint32_t nb_comp)
functions.description: Sets a custom multi-component transform (MCT) matrix and DC shift coefficients in the compression parameters for custom color transforms.
requirements: parameters must be a valid pointer to grk_cparameters to be modified.
encoding_matrix must point to a float matrix suitable for nb_comp components; exact layout is not documented here.
dc_shift must point to an array of nb_comp int32_t values (implied by parameter name).
nb_comp is the number of components; should match the image’s component count used for compression.
Returns true if successfully set; false otherwise.

functions.name: grk_plugin_load
functions.description: Loads a Grok plugin from the specified path, optionally enabling verbose output.
requirements: info.pluginPath should be a valid path to the plugin binary.
Should be called before using plugin-accelerated functions that depend on plugin availability.
Returns true on success; false on failure.

functions.name: grk_plugin_cleanup
functions.description: Cleans up plugin resources loaded via grk_plugin_load.
requirements: Call after plugin use has finished to release resources. Avoid calling plugin-dependent APIs after cleanup unless reloading the plugin.

functions.name: grk_plugin_get_debug_state
functions.description: Returns the current plugin debug state as a bitmask (e.g., GRK_PLUGIN_STATE_NO_DEBUG, GRK_PLUGIN_STATE_DEBUG, GRK_PLUGIN_STATE_PRE_TR1, GRK_PLUGIN_STATE_DWT_QUANTIZATION, GRK_PLUGIN_STATE_MCT_ONLY).
requirements: Callable when a plugin is present; exact behavior without a plugin is unspecified.

functions.name: grk_plugin_init
functions.description: Initializes the plugin with device selection, verbosity, and optional license/server information.
requirements: A plugin should be loaded prior to initialization (implied).
init_info fields (device_id, verbose, license, server) should be set appropriately; semantics of license/server are not detailed here.
Returns true on success; false otherwise.

functions.name: grk_plugin_compress
functions.signature: int32_t GRK_CALLCONV grk_plugin_compress(grk_cparameters* compress_parameters, GRK_PLUGIN_COMPRESS_USER_CALLBACK callback)
functions.description: Runs a plugin-driven compression using the provided compression parameters and a user callback for file-oriented workflows. Returns 0 on success, non-zero error code on failure.
requirements: compress_parameters must be a valid grk_cparameters pointer.
callback must be a valid function pointer of type GRK_PLUGIN_COMPRESS_USER_CALLBACK; it will be invoked with a grk_plugin_compress_user_callback_info pointer.
Plugin must be loaded and initialized (implied by being a plugin entry point).
Caller should interpret non-zero return as an error.

functions.name: grk_plugin_batch_compress
functions.description: Performs batch compression using the plugin across an input directory, writing to an output directory, using provided parameters and optional per-item callback. Returns 0 on success.
requirements: info.input_dir and info.output_dir should be valid directory paths accessible to the process.
info.compress_parameters must be a valid pointer to grk_cparameters.
info.callback, if provided, must conform to GRK_PLUGIN_COMPRESS_USER_CALLBACK.
Returns 0 on success; non-zero indicates failure.

functions.name: grk_plugin_wait_for_batch_complete
functions.description: Blocks until the current plugin batch compression job completes.
requirements: Should only be called after initiating a batch job (e.g., grk_plugin_batch_compress).

functions.name: grk_plugin_stop_batch_compress
functions.description: Requests that the current plugin batch compression job stop.
requirements: Should only be called while a batch compression job is in progress.

functions.name: grk_plugin_decompress
functions.description: Runs a single-image decompression via the plugin, driven by the provided decompression parameters and callback. Returns 0 on success, otherwise an error code.
requirements: decompress_parameters must be a valid pointer to grk_decompress_parameters.
callback must be a valid grk_plugin_decompress_callback function pointer that will be invoked with a grk_plugin_decompress_callback_info pointer.
Returns 0 on success; non-zero error code otherwise.

functions.name: grk_plugin_init_batch_decompress
functions.signature: int32_t GRK_CALLCONV grk_plugin_init_batch_decompress(const char* input_dir, const char* output_dir, grk_decompress_parameters* decompress_parameters, grk_plugin_decompress_callback callback)
functions.description: Initializes a plugin-driven batch decompression job over an input directory to an output directory, with the provided decompression parameters and callback. Returns 0 on success.
requirements: input_dir and output_dir must be valid directory paths accessible to the process.
decompress_parameters must be a valid pointer to grk_decompress_parameters.
callback must be a valid grk_plugin_decompress_callback function pointer.
Returns 0 on success; non-zero indicates failure.

functions.name: grk_plugin_batch_decompress
functions.description: Starts or advances the plugin batch decompression process previously initialized. Returns 0 on success, otherwise an error code.
requirements: Should be called after a successful grk_plugin_init_batch_decompress.
Returns 0 on success; non-zero indicates failure.

functions.name: grk_plugin_stop_batch_decompress
functions.description: Stops the current plugin batch decompression job.
requirements: Should only be called while a batch decompression job is in progress.

unharnessable_functions.name: grk_decompress
unharnessable_functions.reason: Requires a valid grk_plugin_tile structure populated by the plugin pipeline, which cannot be safely constructed within this fuzzer model.

unharnessable_functions.name: grk_decompress_wait
unharnessable_functions.reason: May block indefinitely waiting for asynchronous decode completion, which is unsuitable for a fast fuzzer harness.

unharnessable_functions.name: grk_plugin_load
unharnessable_functions.reason: Requires loading an external plugin binary from the filesystem which is unavailable/uncontrolled in the fuzzer environment.

unharnessable_functions.name: grk_plugin_cleanup
unharnessable_functions.reason: Depends on prior plugin loading and external plugin state which is not available in the fuzzer environment.

unharnessable_functions.name: grk_plugin_get_debug_state
unharnessable_functions.reason: Relies on plugin subsystem presence and state which cannot be guaranteed in the fuzzer environment.

unharnessable_functions.name: grk_plugin_init
unharnessable_functions.reason: Requires an externally loaded plugin and device-specific initialization not available under the fuzzer model.

unharnessable_functions.name: grk_plugin_compress
unharnessable_functions.reason: Depends on an external plugin backend and callback machinery not controllable in the fuzzer environment.

unharnessable_functions.name: grk_plugin_batch_compress
unharnessable_functions.reason: Requires valid filesystem directories and a loaded plugin to operate, which are unavailable to the fuzzer.

unharnessable_functions.name: grk_plugin_wait_for_batch_complete

unharnessable_functions.name: grk_plugin_stop_batch_compress
unharnessable_functions.reason: Assumes an active plugin batch compression job not present in the fuzzer environment.

unharnessable_functions.name: grk_plugin_decompress
unharnessable_functions.reason: Depends on an external plugin backend and callback which are not available in the fuzzer environment.

unharnessable_functions.name: grk_plugin_init_batch_decompress
unharnessable_functions.reason: Requires valid filesystem directories and a loaded plugin to initialize, which are unavailable to the fuzzer.

unharnessable_functions.name: grk_plugin_batch_decompress
unharnessable_functions.reason: Assumes a previously initialized plugin batch job which cannot be established in the fuzzer environment.

unharnessable_functions.name: grk_plugin_stop_batch_decompress
unharnessable_functions.reason: Assumes an active plugin batch decompression job not present in the fuzzer environment.

data_types.description: A string representing a filesystem path to a file or directory. May include absolute or relative paths, separators appropriate to the OS, and typical path characters. In this context it is used as a plugin path for loading a plugin binary.

generators.generator:
import os
import random
import string
from typing import List

# Data type: filesystem path string used as pluginPath for grk_initialize
# Fuzzer stub behavior:
# - FUZZ_PARAM_STR() is used to supply a candidate pluginPath string.
# - The stub may replace it with nullptr 1/3 of the time, so our buffer should still be
#   a plausible path string when used.
# Goal:
# - Generate a bytes buffer that represents an interesting, valid filesystem path string.
# - Include variations: absolute/relative, different separators, with/without extension,
#   nested directories, environment-like segments, Unicode, spaces, dots, hidden paths,
#   long segments, edge names like . and .., and typical plugin extensions (.so/.dll/.dylib).
# - Keep size <= 4096 bytes.
# - Deterministic per seed but random across seeds.

MAX_LEN = 1024

_windows_exts = [".dll"]
_posix_exts = [".so", ".so.1", ".so.0", ".so.2"]
_macos_exts = [".dylib"]

# Common directory names and components that appear in plugin paths
DIR_NAMES = [
    "plugins", "bin", "lib", "lib64", "build", "cmake", "out", "Release", "Debug",
    "grok", "grok-plugin", "jpeg2000", "opencv", "third_party", "usr", "local", "opt",
    "Program Files", "AppData", "Roaming", "Library", "Frameworks", "Contents", "Resources",
]

BASENAMES = [
    "grok", "grok_plugin", "jpeg2000", "jp2", "codec", "accel", "compute",
    "mct", "dwt", "quant", "color", "io", "plugin", "device",
]

UNICODE_SEGMENTS = [
    "πlug", "プラグイン", "插件", "плагин", "دعم", "プラグ", "插件库", "δοκιμή",
]

SPECIAL_SEGMENTS = [".", "..", "-", "_", "~", "hidden", ".hidden", "#temp", "$cache"]

DRIVES = ["C:", "D:", "E:"]

SEP_WIN = "\\"
SEP_POSIX = "/"


def _rand_choice(r: random.Random, items: List[str]) -> str:
    return items[r.randrange(len(items))]


def _random_name(r: random.Random) -> str:
    parts = []
    # mix of base, digits, and unicode occasionally
    base = _rand_choice(r, BASENAMES)
    parts.append(base)
    if r.random() < 0.5:
        parts.append(str(r.randrange(0, 100)))
    if r.random() < 0.2:
        parts.append(_rand_choice(r, UNICODE_SEGMENTS))
    name = "-".join(parts)
    # occasionally add underscores
    if r.random() < 0.3:
        name = name.replace("-", "_")
    return name


def _random_ext(r: random.Random, flavor: str) -> str:
    if flavor == "windows":
        pool = _windows_exts
    elif flavor == "macos":
        pool = _macos_exts + _posix_exts
    else:
        pool = _posix_exts
    return _rand_choice(r, pool)


def _make_windows_path(r: random.Random) -> str:
    # Choose drive or UNC
    if r.random() < 0.2:
        # UNC path
        server = _random_name(r)
        share = _random_name(r)
        prefix = f"\\\\{server}{SEP_WIN}{share}"
    else:
        prefix = _rand_choice(r, DRIVES)
    segments = []
    depth = r.randint(1, 6)
    for _ in range(depth):
        choice_pool = DIR_NAMES + SPECIAL_SEGMENTS + UNICODE_SEGMENTS
        seg = _rand_choice(r, choice_pool)
        # sanitize separators for Windows
        seg = seg.replace(SEP_POSIX, "-").replace(SEP_WIN, "-")
        segments.append(seg)
    base = _random_name(r)
    ext = _random_ext(r, "windows") if r.random() < 0.9 else ""
    leaf = base + ext
    path = prefix + SEP_WIN + SEP_WIN.join(segments + [leaf])
    # Occasionally add quotes or spaces inside segments already handled; ensure no trailing space
    return path


def _make_posix_path(r: random.Random, flavor: str) -> str:
    absolute = r.random() < 0.7
    prefix = SEP_POSIX if absolute else ""
    segments = []
    depth = r.randint(1, 7)
    for i in range(depth):
        pool = DIR_NAMES + SPECIAL_SEGMENTS + UNICODE_SEGMENTS
        seg = _rand_choice(r, pool)
        seg = seg.replace(SEP_POSIX, "-").replace(SEP_WIN, "-")
        # hide some dirs
        if r.random() < 0.2 and not seg.startswith('.'):
            seg = "." + seg
        segments.append(seg)
    base = _random_name(r)
    ext = _random_ext(r, flavor) if r.random() < 0.95 else ""
    leaf = base + ext
    # Occasionally put versioned suffix
    if r.random() < 0.3:
        leaf += f".{r.randint(0,3)}.{r.randint(0,9)}"
    path = prefix + SEP_POSIX.join(segments + [leaf])
    return path


def _maybe_env_prefix(r: random.Random, s: str, flavor: str) -> str:
    if r.random() < 0.25:
        if flavor == "windows":
            envs = ["%PROGRAMFILES%", "%APPDATA%", "%LOCALAPPDATA%", "%USERPROFILE%"]
            return _rand_choice(r, envs) + SEP_WIN + s
        else:
            envs = ["$HOME", "$PWD", "$TMPDIR", "~"]
            sep = SEP_POSIX
            # ~ already expands to home without separator
            if s.startswith(sep):
                return _rand_choice(r, envs) + s
            return _rand_choice(r, envs) + sep + s
    return s


def _maybe_trailing_sep(r: random.Random, s: str, flavor: str) -> str:
    if r.random() < 0.1:
        return s + (SEP_WIN if flavor == "windows" else SEP_POSIX)
    return s


def generate(seed: int) -> bytes:
    r = random.Random(seed)
    # Choose OS flavor to vary path styles
    flavor = r.choice(["windows", "posix", "macos"])  # macos uses posix separators

    if flavor == "windows":
        path = _make_windows_path(r)
    else:
        path = _make_posix_path(r, flavor)

    # Optionally prepend environment-like prefix
    path = _maybe_env_prefix(r, path, flavor)

    # Optionally add trailing separator (directories as plugin path roots)
    path = _maybe_trailing_sep(r, path, flavor)

    # Ensure overall length constraints
    if len(path) > MAX_LEN:
        path = path[:MAX_LEN]

    # Return as UTF-8 bytes; include NUL rarely to simulate C-string termination inside buffer
    if r.random() < 0.05:
        path += "\x00"
    return path.encode("utf-8", errors="ignore")
